title: Client-side graceful degradation blueprint
content:
Purpose and quick context:

This is a personal design scratchpad that pulls together a lightweight client-side blueprint for graceful degradation when server-side inference is degraded, slow, or expensive. The focus is the client (SDK/browser/edge) behaviour, not server internals.

Goals:
- Maintain a useful user experience under partial outages or high-latency conditions.
- Provide deterministic, auditable fallback behaviour so product teams can reason about quality and cost tradeoffs.
- Keep the client implementation small and pluggable for both web SDK and mobile/native clients.

Non-goals:
- Replacing server-side fallback/autoscaling strategies.
- Full security/audit spec for enterprise/private deployments (separate doc).

Assumptions:
- The Redwood API supports route-level fallbacks and returns structured telemetry and enforcement hints in headers (x-rw-fallback, x-rw-latency-hint).
- The client SDK can persist a small local cache (indexeddb/sqlite) and has limited compute for cheap on-device models (e.g., tiny embedding or heuristic).
- Product owners can supply a fallback prompt template or simple heuristic function.

Failure modes we handle:
1) Increased p95/p99 latency (service slow)
2) 5xx errors or partial errors (model fails)
3) Rate-limiting/quota enforcement on the server side
4) Cost-heavy model selected unexpectedly

User experience tiers (recommended):
- Fast-path: normal request -> server returns within latency SLO -> full result
- Stale-accept: server accepts request but latency exceeds threshold T_stale -> UI shows progressive result placeholder + optional cached result then final replacement
- Local-fallback: server unreachable/5xx or rate limit -> run fallback handler (cache hit or lightweight local model/heuristic)
- Offline-grace: no network -> show last-successful result or compact summary + soft-disable expensive features

Client architecture (components):
- Transport layer: abstracts fetch with retry, circuit-breaker, and telemetry hooks.
- Fallback policy engine: declarative policy that maps server signals + client state -> action (wait, fallback, degrade).
- Local cache: small LRU store keyed by request fingerprint and prompt template. TTLs and usage caps configurable.
- Policy config store: CDN-updatable JSON configs with local overrides.
- Telemetry emitter: batched ping to telemetry backend with event types (fallback_decision, cache_hit, server_latency_exceeded).

Tiny ASCII diagram:

Client App
  |--> SDK(fallback-policy)
         |--> transport(fetch with circuit)
         |--> cache (indexdb/sqlite)
         |--> local-model shim (optional)
  |--> UI (progressive placeholders)

Policy DSL (sketch) - small, expressive JSON not YAML to fit SDKs:

{
  "version": "1",
  "routes": {
    "chat.generate": {
      "latency_slo_ms": 300,
      "stale_threshold_ms": 700,
      "fallback_sequence": ["cache", "local_heuristic", "server_retry"],
      "circuit_breaker": {
        "window_ms": 60000,
        "failure_threshold": 0.1,
        "min_calls": 30,
        "open_for_ms": 30000
      }
    }
  },
  "global": {
    "max_cache_size": 150000, // bytes
    "telemetry_batch_ms": 5000
  }
}

Notes on fields:
- stale_threshold_ms: after this elapse, SDK should surface an interim UI and optionally use cache result while awaiting server.
- fallback_sequence: ordered handlers; SDK tries each until it gets a result. Handler types: cache, local_heuristic, local_model, server_retry, minimal_stub.

API shape for fallback-aware request headers (client -> server):
- X-RW-Client-Request-Id: uuid
- X-RW-Client-Timeout-Ms: int (soft timeout for server)
- X-RW-Fallback-Mode: allow|prefer-local|require-local|none

Server hints in response headers (server -> client):
- X-RW-Server-Latency-Hint: fast|moderate|slow
- X-RW-Fallback-Advised: cache|local_heuristic|local_model|none
- X-RW-Model-Cost-Score: low|medium|high (heuristic for client to decide whether to use costly model)

Circuit-breaker behaviour (sketch):
- Track rolling window of calls and failures. Failure = 5xx, timeout > client soft timeout, or explicit server-advised degrade.
- If failure_rate > failure_threshold and calls >= min_calls => open circuit.
- When open, short-circuit to fallback_sequence immediately and emit telemetry.
- After open_for_ms, probe with single request (half-open); success => close, failure => re-open with exponential backoff.

Local fallback handlers (examples):
- cache: exact fingerprint match -> return stored full response
- cache-approx: fuzzy match of last N responses by semantic embedding (cheap approximate) -> return snippet + "possibly stale" flag
- local_heuristic: run template-based filler (stub) that produces short helpful text (e.g., summary of last-known context)
- local_model: small on-device transformer (quantized) that handles simple prompts (only for apps that bundle it)
- minimal_stub: short apology + action buttons (try again, view cached answer, go offline view)

Cache fingerprinting (suggested):
- fingerprint = sha1( route + prompt_template_id + truncated_context_hash + user_locale + feature_flags )
- TTLs: route-specific; defaults: chat.generate -> 10m, embeddings -> 24h (for embedding reuse), rerank -> 2m.

Telemetry events (minimum fields):
- event_type: fallback_taken|cache_hit|cache_miss|circuit_opened|circuit_closed|probe_result
- timestamp
- client_request_id
- route
- decision_path: ["cache","local_heuristic"]
- latency_ms
- debug_hint: server_header_values (optional)

UX guidance (short):
- For stale results, show a skeleton with subtle label "result may be stale" and provide a refresh affordance.
- For local heuristics, mark clearly as "quick summary" with ability to request full server answer.
- Avoid hiding fallback state entirely; telemetry needs to be linked to product metrics so PMs can measure quality regressions.

Edge cases and tradeoffs:
- Privacy: local_model and cache should encrypt sensitive context; provide opt-out.
- Consistency: fallback responses can diverge; add provenance metadata so downstream systems can treat them differently.
- Cost: local_model reduces server cost but increases app size. Provide toggle at build-time or via feature flag.

Rollout checklist for product teams:
- [ ] Add SDK flag to enable client graceful degradation (off by default)
- [ ] Author route-level policy JSON with sane defaults
- [ ] Instrument telemetry and test capture of fallback events
- [ ] UX copy for each fallback tier ready and reviewed
- [ ] Beta release to subset of users with override to force degraded behaviour for testing

Open questions (for follow-up):
- Should the server expose a canonical "fallback_score" per response that encodes both cost and quality? Useful for client decisions but tricky to calibrate.
- How to best version/update policy JSON in older clients? Consider a ttl-on-config with migration-safe defaults.
- Is it acceptable for product teams to opt for local_model on mobile without explicit security review? Need policy.

Next steps (personal):
1) Prototype a tiny SDK shim that implements the circuit-breaker + cache path (2–3 days).
2) Run a tabletop sim with synthetic latency/failure traces and gather p95/p99 user-visible change.
3) Write short RFC for platform teams describing headers and hints so server can start emitting them.

Notes-to-self: keep this as a compact building block paper — goal is a 1–2 file SDK drop + a lightweight policy JSON that product teams can tweak.

-- Ana
